candidate_reviews.strongest_counterargument: Total restriction does not fully capture QMA2 versus QMA; restricted protocols can progress without resolving the class.
Restricted Hamiltonian results need not resolve whole-class simulation.
Promise-complete and cryptographic motivations are only partly represented by a total row.
Logspace error variants compete for the same scientific program.
Uses a cross-field slot; individual numerical algorithms need not settle BQL versus BPL.
The total inclusion is weaker than the canonical promise conjecture; reduction choice matters.
Exact gate convention is part of the question, not a harmless implementation choice.
Protocol/setup variants can crowd out other computational resources.
Nearby existing anchors already capture some questions; two-message refinement has opportunity cost.

findings.impact: A fixed perfect-soundness slice cannot be substituted for the intended general StoqMA endpoint.
findings.action: Use an explicit efficiently computable inverse-polynomial-gap parameter union, or cite an equivalence for a different chosen parameter convention.

findings.statement: NOT/CNOT/Toffoli, zero/plus ancillas, one final X-basis measurement; generic QMA amplification is not licensed.
findings.impact: Choosing 2/3 versus 1/3 or claiming arbitrary parameter equivalence changes the class.
findings.action: Bind allowed gates, measurements, rational threshold representation, and quantifier order.

findings.statement: Promise inclusion implies total inclusion; total separation implies promise separation. The converse directions need extra arguments.
findings.impact: Canonical QMA/QCMA/QPCP promise questions are not fully represented by total restrictions.
findings.action: Use typed bridge theorems rather than erasing promise annotations.

findings.statement: Total NEXP inclusion in total QMA2 gives the corresponding promise inclusion via the acceptance language of the bounded NEXP machine.
findings.impact: The NEXP versus QMA2 extreme comparison is faithfully represented by the total pair.
findings.action: Require the standard all-input exponential machine bound; do not generalize completion to gapped quantum classes.

findings.statement: The cited model measures successive proof indices and restricts operations to workspace and already accessed proof qubits.
findings.impact: An unspecified global quantum query gate is not the cited constant-access verifier.
findings.action: Fix one proof, constant-query union, uniformity, bounded error, and the reduction convention.

findings.statement: The cited QMA1 model fixes H,T,CNOT; approximate universality does not establish exact-completeness equivalence.
findings.impact: Different gate conventions can name a different target.
findings.action: Gate model and projector input encoding must precede cutoff audit.

findings.verdict: accept and give greater total-track weight
findings.statement: Theorem4 in Apers–Edenhofer is a total language with the path-bound condition checked, not just promised.
findings.impact: BQL has direct total-language motivation separate from BQP.
findings.action: Preserve polynomial runtime, logarithmic total work/control space, and space-bounded uniformity.

findings.statement: Two product witness registers, polynomial size, and standard gap; amplification theorem must be matched to its regime.
findings.impact: Short-witness, vanishing-gap, or different bipartition variants cannot be transferred by name.
findings.action: Keep product-state soundness; do not assume arbitrary entangled repetition is independent.

counting_algebra_cross_check.proof: Fix A in P^PP and its fixed B in PP. Inline the deterministic B-oracle decider for each A-query in the outer PP machine. Query lengths and compositions remain polynomial; no fresh random branches appear; acceptance is unchanged on every original random tape.
counting_algebra_cross_check.second_equivalence_detail: With D=P^PP and C2=PP^PP, C2=D gives C3=PP^D=C2, hence all higher levels stabilize. Reverse follows from D subset C2 subset CH.
counting_algebra_cross_check.proof_status: independently reasoned mathematical derivation; not yet a Lean certificate or canonical rule
